info.description: Boltzmann brains over REST: discovery, and the full lifecycle -- create, evidence, commits, branches, push/pull, converge, import -- over the service's working store. Lifecycle errors carry a stable `code`: `usage` (400), `not_found` (404), `refused_protocol` (422), `refused_policy` (403), `rejected_candidates` (422), `not_fast_forward` (409), `registry_unavailable` (502), `needs_human` (409), `internal` (500). Long operations answer 202 with a job (`GET /v1/jobs/{id}`).
info.title: Gaussia Brains MCP Server

get.description:
Return detail for a single brain.

A brain held in the working store reports its status: modules and block
counts, head, branches, any open convergence, and its publication, with
the branch head as ``ETag`` (send it back as ``If-Match``). Any other
brain reports its published manifest.

*brain_ref* may be a short reference such as ``brains/my-brain:latest`` or a
full OCI reference such as ``registry.example.com/acme/handbook:main``.

post.description:
Push a branch to its tag (main → the default tag, others → `br.<name>`).

A push of main also indexes the brain in its namespace.

Validate the client's candidates and commit them, all or nothing.

``dry_run`` returns every verdict and writes nothing. A commit whose
candidates did not all validate is ``rejected_candidates`` (422) with the
report; otherwise the committed blocks and the new snapshot.

Migrate an existing brain into the working store (job).

``application/json`` (:class:`ImportRequest`) imports from the registry;
``multipart/form-data`` with a ``layout`` file (a ``.tar``/``.tar.gz`` of a
brain's OCI layout) imports an upload. Governed brains are imported as they
are and served read-only.
